sanskrit: (sod akrāmat) sā vanaspatīn āgacchat tāṃ vanaspatayo 'ghnata sā saṃvatsare sam abhavat | tasmāt saṃvatsare vanaspatīnāṃ vṛkṇam api rohati vṛścyanty asyāpriyaṃ bhrātṛvyaṃ ya (evaṃ veda) ||
english: She went forth; she came to the forest-trees, the forest-trees smote her, and she became whole in a year. Therefore in a year even a felled tree of the forest grows again. They strike down the unloved rival of him who knows this.

sanskrit: (…) sā pitṝn āgacchat tāṃ pitaro 'ghnata sā māse sam abhavat | tasmān māse pitṛbhyo dadati svadhāvān pitṛṣu bhavati pra pitṛyāṇaṃ panthāṃ jānāti yaḥ (…) ||
english: She came to the Pitṛs, the Pitṛs smote her, and she became whole in a month. Therefore in a month they make offerings to the Pitṛs; one who does so becomes possessor of svadhā among the Pitṛs and knows well the path of the Pitṛyāṇa—he who knows this.

sanskrit: (…) sā devān āgacchat tāṃ devā aghnata sārdhamāse sam abhavat | tasmād ardhamāse devebhyo juhvati juhoty agnihotraṃ pra devayānaṃ panthāṃ jānāti yaḥ (…) ||
english: She came to the gods, the gods smote her, and she became whole in a half-month. Therefore in a half-month they offer to the gods; one offers the Agnihotra and knows well the path of the Devayāna—he who knows this.

sanskrit: (…) sā manuṣyān āgacchat tāṃ manuṣyā aghnata sā sadyaḥ sam abhavat | tasmād ubhayadyur manuṣyā upa haranty upāsya gṛhe haranti yaḥ (…) ||
english: She came to human beings, human beings smote her, and she became whole that very day. Therefore on both days humans bring offerings; they bring them reverently into the house—he who knows this.

sanskrit: sod akrāmat sāsurān āgacchat tām asurā upāhvayanta māya ehīti | tasyā virocanaḥ prāhrādur vatsa āsīd ayaspātraṃ pātram | tāṃ dvimūrdhārtviyo 'dhok tāṃ māyām adhok | tāṃ māyām asurā upa jīvanty upajīvanīyo bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
english: She went forth; she came to the Asuras. The Asuras called out to her: 'O Māyā, come!' Her calf was Virocana son of Prahrāda, and her pail was of iron. Dvimūrdhan the Ārtvijaḥ milked her; he milked forth Māyā. On that Māyā the Asuras subsist. He becomes one on whom others subsist—he who knows this.

sanskrit: (…) sā pitṝn āgacchat tāṃ pitara upāhvayanta svadha ehīti | tasyā yamo vaivasvato vatsa āsīd rajatapātraṃ pātram | tām antako mārtayo 'dhok tāṃ svadhām adhok | tāṃ svadhāṃ pitara upa (…) ||
english: She came to the Pitṛs. The Pitṛs called out to her: 'O Svadhā, come!' Her calf was Yama Vaivasvata, and her pail was of silver. Antaka son of Mṛtyu milked her; he milked forth Svadhā. On that Svadhā the Pitṛs subsist—he who knows this.

sanskrit: (…) sā manuṣyān āgacchat tāṃ manuṣyā upāhvayanterāvaty ehīti | tasyā manur vaivasvato vatsa āsīt pṛthivīpātraṃ pātram | tāṃ pṛthur vainyo 'dhok tāṃ kṛṣiṃ ca sasyaṃ cādhok | tāṃ kṛṣiṃ ca sasyaṃ ca manuṣya upa (…) ||
english: She came to human beings. Human beings called out to her: 'O Irāvatī, come!' Her calf was Manu Vaivasvata, and her pail was the earth. Pṛthu son of Vena milked her; he milked forth both ploughing and grain. On that ploughing and grain human beings subsist—he who knows this.

sanskrit: (…) sā devān āgacchat tāṃ devā upāhvayantorja ehīti | tasyā indro vatsa āsīd dārupātraṃ pātram | tāṃ savitādhok tām ūrjam adhok | tām ūrjaṃ devā upa (…) ||
english: She came to the gods. The gods called out to her: 'O Ūrjā, come!' Her calf was Indra, and her pail was of wood. Savitṛ milked her; he milked forth Ūrjā. On that Ūrjā the gods subsist—he who knows this.

sanskrit: (…) sā sapta ṛṣīn āgacchat tāṃ sapta ṛṣaya upāhvayanta brahmaṇvaty ehīti | tasyāḥ somo vatsa āsīc chandaḥpātraṃ pātram | tāṃ bṛhaspatir āṅgiraso 'dhok tāṃ brahma ca tapaś cādhok | tad brahma ca tapaś ca sapta ṛṣaya upa (…) ||
english: She came to the Seven Sages. The Seven Sages called out to her: 'O Brahmaṇvatī, come!' Her calf was Soma, and her pail was the metres. Bṛhaspati of the lineage of Āṅgiras milked her; he milked forth both brahman and tapas. On that brahman and tapas the Seven Sages subsist—he who knows this.

sanskrit: (…) sā gandharvāpsarasa āgacchat tāṃ gandharvāpsarasa upāhvayanta puṇyagandha ehīti | tasyāś citrarathaḥ sauryavarcaso vatsa āsīt puṣkaraparṇaṃ pātram | tāṃ vasuruciḥ sauryavarcaso 'dhok tāṃ puṇyaṃ gandham adhok | taṃ puṇyaṃ gandhaṃ gandharvāpsarasā upa (…) ||
english: She came to the Gandharvas and Apsarasas. The Gandharvas and Apsarasas called out to her: 'O Puṇyagandhā, come!' Her calf was Citraratha son of Sūryavarcas, and her pail was a lotus leaf. Vasurucis son of Sūryavarcas milked her; he milked forth the holy fragrance. On that holy fragrance the Gandharvas and Apsarasas subsist—he who knows this.

sanskrit: (…) sā puṇyajanān āgacchat tāṃ puṇyajanā upāhvayanta tirodha ehīti | tasyāḥ kubero vaiśravaṇo vatsa āsīd āmapātraṃ pātram | tāṃ rajatanābhiḥ kāberako 'dhok tāṃ tirodhām adhok | tāṃ tirodhāṃ puṇyajanā upa (…) ||
english: She came to the Puṇyajanas. The Puṇyajanas called out to her: 'O Tirodhā, come!' Her calf was Kubera Vaiśravaṇa, and her pail was of unbaked clay. Rajatanābhi the Kāberaka milked her; he milked forth invisibility. On that invisibility the Puṇyajanas subsist—he who knows this.

sanskrit: sod akrāmat sā sarpān āgacchat tāṃ sarpā upāhvayanta viṣavaty ehīti | tasyās takṣako vaiśāleyo vatsa āsīd alābupātraṃ pātram | tāṃ dhṛtarāṣṭra airāvato 'dhok tāṃ viṣam adhok | tad viṣaṃ sarpā upa jīvanty upajīvanīyo bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
english: She went forth; she came to the Serpents. The Serpents called out to her: 'O Viṣavatī, come!' Her calf was Takṣaka of Vaiśāla, and her pail was a gourd vessel. Dhṛtarāṣṭra son of Airāvata milked her; he milked forth venom. On that venom the Serpents subsist. He becomes one on whom others subsist—he who knows this.

sanskrit: tasmād yasmā alābunābhiṣiñcen manasā tvā pratyāhanmīty enaṃ pratyāhanyāt | yat pratyāhanti viṣaṃ pratyāhanti na ca pratyāhanti viṣam anu prasicyate | viṣam asyāpriyaṃ bhrātṛvyaṃ hanti ya evaṃ veda ||
english: Therefore upon whomsoever one sprinkles with a gourd vessel, saying in the mind 'I strike you back,' let him strike that one back. What one strikes back is venom he strikes back; yet when one does not strike it back, the venom flows on after him. He slays the venom, the unloved rival of him—he who knows this.

sanskrit: aghāyatām api nahyā mukhāni sapatneṣu vajram arpayaitam | indreṇa dattā prathamā śataudanā bhrātṛvyaghnī yajamānāya gātuḥ ||
english: Bind shut the mouths of those who scheme evil; hurl this thunderbolt upon the rivals. The first Śataudanā, given by Indra, slays rivals and clears the way for the sacrificer.

sanskrit: vediṣ ṭe carma bhavatu barhir lomāni yāni te | eṣā tvā raśanāgrahīd grāvā tvaiṣo 'dhi nṛtyatu ||
english: Let the altar-ground be your hide, let the sacrificial grass be your body-hair. This halter has seized you; let this pressing-stone dance upon you.

sanskrit: bālās te prokṣaṇīḥ santu jihvā saṃ mārṣṭv aghnye | śuddhā tvaṃ yajñiyā bhūtvā divaṃ prehi śataudane ||
english: Let your tail-hairs be the sprinkling-waters; let your tongue lick the altar-grass, O inviolable one. Pure, having become fit for sacrifice, go to heaven, O Śataudanā.

sanskrit: yaḥ śataudanāṃ pacati kāmapreṇa sa kalpate | prītā hy asya ṛtvijaḥ sarve yanti yathāyatham ||
english: He who cooks the Śataudanā with love fulfils his purpose; for his officiating priests, well pleased, all go each to his proper place.

sanskrit: ye te devi śamitāras tvaṃ paktāro ye ca te janāḥ | ete tvā sarve gopsyanti maibhyo bhaiṣīḥ śataudane ||
english: O goddess, your slaughterers and those persons who are your cooks—all these will protect you; do not be afraid of them, O Śataudanā.

sanskrit: sa svargam ā rohati yatrādas tridivaṃ divaḥ | hiraṇyajyotiṣaṃ kṛtvā yo dadāti śataudanām ||
english: He ascends to heaven, to yonder triple heaven of the sky, making it resplendent with gold—he who gives the Śataudanā.

sanskrit: sa tāṃl lokān sam āpnoti yeṣu devāḥ samāsate | apūpaṃ nābhiṃ kṛtvā yo dadāti śataudanām ||
english: He attains fully those worlds in which the gods dwell, making an apūpa cake its navel—he who gives the Śataudanā.

sanskrit: vasavas tvā dakṣiṇata uttarān marutas tvā | ādityāḥ paścād gopsyanti sātirātram agniṣṭomam ati drava ||
english: The Vasus will guard you from the south, the Maruts from the north; the Ādityas will guard you from the west. Run beyond the Agniṣṭoma with the Atirātra.

sanskrit: gandharvā apsaraso devi rudrā aṅgirasas tvā | ete tvā sarve gopsyanti sātirātram agniṣṭomam ati drava ||
english: The Gandharvas, the Apsarasas, O goddess, the Rudras, the Āṅgirasas will guard you. All these will protect you. Run beyond the Agniṣṭoma with the Atirātra.

sanskrit: antarikṣaṃ divaṃ bhūmim ādityān maruto diśaḥ | lokān sarvān āpnoti yo dadāti śataudanām ||
english: The atmosphere, the sky, the earth, the Ādityas, the Maruts, the directions—all the worlds he attains—he who gives the Śataudanā.
